sections.h2: Where is the Sumner County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office is at 355 N. Belvedere Drive, Suite 201, Gallatin, TN 37066. Call 615-452-3892 or fax 615-442-1105. Counter hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday. The register is an elected officer with a four-year term, and the staff is eight people plus the register.

The same building houses the Assessor of Property in Room 206 and the Trustee in Room 107, which makes it easy to check a parcel's value and tax status on the way to or from the recording counter.

The register's county page says the office records more than 30,000 legal documents in a typical fiscal year and handles over eighty types of instrument under the recording statutes.

sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Sumner County?
sections.html:
Sumner County is on Tennessee's northern edge, 25 miles northeast of Nashville. Its 543 square miles hold eight cities: Gallatin, the county seat, Hendersonville, Goodlettsville, Millersville, Mitchellville, Portland, Westmoreland and White House. Bledsoe Creek State Park sits on Old Hickory Lake, part of the Cumberland River system that shaped early trade here.

The county was organized in 1786, and the early forts at Mansker's Station, Bledsoe's Station and Asher's Station anchored its first settlements. Volunteer State Community College and a Union University campus in Hendersonville add to the local base.

Census Bureau QuickFacts for the market side:

  • 215,538 people in July 2025, up 9.8% since April 2020
  • 89,138 housing units, with 72.0% owner-occupied
  • Median owner-occupied value of $393,100 (2020 to 2024)
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage of $1,831
  • 3,045 building permits in 2025

At the median value, Tennessee's $0.37-per-$100 transfer tax would come to about $1,454 on a sale in Sumner County.

sections.h2: What records can I search through the Sumner County register?
sections.html:
The register's office says its records are certified back to September 1989 and searchable online at ustitlesearch.net. Deed books and indexes going back to 1786 have been digitized, so an older chain of title can be traced without a trip to Gallatin. A public search room is also open at the office.

Free fraud monitoring is available through MyLandAlert, which the register runs with ProGResS, Inc. It emails an owner when a document is recorded under his or her name or business, an early warning for forged deeds and mortgage fraud.

sections.h2: Can a Sumner County deed be e-recorded?
sections.html:
Yes, through two vendors named by the register: Simplifile, Inc. and CSC eRecording Solutions. The office describes e-recording as faster than paper, with documents received, recorded and returned in a short time. Tennessee limits who may submit electronically to professionals such as attorneys, lenders and title companies, so a seller will normally rely on the one handling the sale.

Paper filings still work in person or by mail at Suite 201. Bring the original, signed and notarized deed with the fees. For the exact recording fee on a given document, call 615-452-3892 before you send it.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees apply when recording a Sumner County sale deed?
sections.html:
The register collects the state conveyance tax and mortgage tax together with recording fees. State taxes go to the Department of Revenue every month, and the county keeps the recording fees. The state rates are:

State recordation taxes collected at the Sumner County register
TaxRateSource
Realty transfer tax$0.37 per $100 of purchase priceTennessee Department of Revenue
Mortgage tax$0.115 per $100 of debt, first $2,000 exemptTennessee Department of Revenue

Check the purchase contract for who covers the tax. State law also lists no-tax transfers, such as an executor's deed under a will or a divorce settlement deed, and the Shelby County register's guidelines spell out that list. For a new loan the lender's deed of trust carries the mortgage tax, and the payoff release of an old loan is recorded after closing.

sections.h2: What does the Sumner County register need on a deed?
sections.html:
A recorded deed has to carry the details Tennessee Code requires, and the Shelby County register's published list shows the usual set. Typical items include:

  • Grantor and grantee names and a legal description
  • A derivation clause naming the prior recorded deed
  • Owner and tax-payer name and address, plus the preparer's name and address
  • The parcel number and, if taxable, a sworn statement of value
  • A notarized acknowledgment of the signature

The register does not draft documents or give legal advice, and a deed missing an item can be turned away. A closing attorney or title company usually checks this list.

sections.h2: Does it matter which part of a Sumner County city the house is in?
sections.html:
It can. Goodlettsville lies partly in Davidson County, and Millersville, Portland and White House each reach into Robertson County. A mailing address with a Sumner city name does not prove the parcel is inside Sumner County. Confirm the county on the Assessor's property search or the deed's parcel number before choosing a register's office, and ask the title company which county will receive the filing.

Gallatin, the county seat, is where the courthouse offices sit. Early military history left marks on its streets: the Union commander Eleazer A. Paine ran his garrison from Gallatin during the Civil War, and houses from that era still stand.

sections.h2: How does Sumner County compare with other Tennessee counties for sellers?
sections.html:
The Census numbers set Sumner County apart from the other two large Tennessee counties covered in this series. Its median owner-occupied value of $393,100 is well above Shelby County's $249,100 and Sullivan County's $213,300, and its median household income of $90,301 is the highest of the three. Population growth since 2020 is 9.8 percent, while Shelby lost 2.1 percent.

For a seller, higher values mean larger recording taxes, since the $0.37-per-$100 rate scales with price. The recording fee itself stays small in comparison, so the tax drives the closing-table total.

sections.h2: How does the register connect to Sumner County property tax?
sections.html: Recording a deed updates the owner of record but does not pay anything. Sumner County taxes become due the first Monday in October and are delinquent after February 28. Ask the Trustee at 615-452-1260 for the parcel balance before closing, and tell the Assessor at 615-452-2412 where the new owner wants the bill mailed.

faqs.q: What are the Sumner County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., at 355 N. Belvedere Drive, Suite 201, Gallatin. The phone number is 615-452-3892.
Yes. The register accepts e-recorded documents through Simplifile, Inc. and CSC eRecording Solutions. Most sellers will use a title company that already has an account.

faqs.q: How far back do Sumner County online records go?
faqs.a: The register's records are certified back to September 1989 and searchable online. Deed books and indexes back to 1786 have been digitized.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a Sumner County sale?
faqs.a: Tennessee charges $0.37 per $100 of the purchase price, collected by the register when the deed is recorded. On a $400,000 sale that is $1,480.

faqs.q: Can I get alerts about filings under my name in Sumner County?
faqs.a: Yes. MyLandAlert is free and emails you when a document is recorded under your name or business.
